newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand dollar closes flat, seen edging higher.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand dollar closes flat, seen edging higher.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed a touch firmer on Wednesday but failed to recover from its overnight fall after lower-than-expected inflation data sparked an easing in monetary conditions.
The Kiwi closed at US$0.6869/74 and at 68.38 on its Trade-Weighted Index, little changed from its 0.6862/69 and 68.41 open.
"It looks like the market is a little bit short and the Aussie has also moved to its highs for the day -- that should help the Kiwi drag up a bit," a dealer said.

The Kiwi fell from 69 U.S. cents prior to the release of March quarter inflation data on Tuesday, which at 0.22 percent for the quarter and 1.97 percent for the year were significantly below market and central bank expectations.
Dealers said a 2.4 percent fall in February retail trade statistics, released on Wednesday, had contributed to the picture of a slowing economy and kept the Kiwi under pressure.
"It's been pretty quiet really. There was a gradual drift down from yesterday and retail sales came out worse than expected," said the dealer.
He said the local market sold the currency after the mid-morning retail trade release and it fell to 0.6860 before Asian buying interest lifted it back to around its opening levels.
The Kiwi was seen trading a 0.6860-85 range overnight.
